newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends defensive on Thai problems.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends defensive on Thai problems.

text.p: * Central Bank raises overnight borrowing twice to 13 pct
The problems of the Thai baht kept the Philippine peso defensive on Thursday, forcing the Central Bank to raise its borrowing rate twice and to sell more dollars at the close, traders said.
The peso ended unchanged at 26.375 to the dollar, the rate at which the Central Bank had been selling dollars during the day.
The Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing by a total of 1.75 percentage points to 13 percent to protect the peso.
But even after raising its rate twice, traders said the Central Bank had to unload more dollars at the close.
"Banks were still jittery because of the volatility in the region," a foreign bank dealer said.
Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza told Reuters the Central Bank was a net seller of dollars on Thursday but it was not a significant amount since it also bought dollars during the day.
A dealer estimated the Central Bank had net sales of $49 million with total sales at $97 million and purchases at $48 million.
Volume was higher than usual at $307.8 million.
Traders said the market could calm down on Friday as long as the Central Bank stayed firm on its offer rate for the dollar at 26.375.
